title: Bidirectional A* on SF: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* shrink search time by running two A* frontiers—one from the start and one from the goal—until they meet. This mirrors how routing AI can compute fast paths on dense city graphs.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm ⚡ How autonomous vehicle routing calculates optimal paths in milliseconds. 

In this visualization, the algorithm launches two simultaneous A* searches:
• Forward A* from your start node
• Backward A* from the destination
When the frontiers meet, we stitch the route together—often exploring far fewer streets than one-direction A*. 

Key idea (why it’s fast): both searches use heuristics (estimated distance-to-goal) to stay “goal-directed,” but dividing the work reduces the explored state space.

Takeaway: Fewer expanded nodes = faster route decisions on real maps (especially in large, grid-like street graphs).

Debate question: Should autonomous routing always optimize strictly for shortest distance, or should it incorporate real-time risk/traffic too?
